headline: US SLAMS 🇺🇸 Australia's ALGO 🍔 Opt-Out LAWS 📜 as 'CENSORSHIP' 🚫
text:
US 🇺🇸 embassy 🏛️ in Canberra 🦘 just DROPPED 💣 a spicy 🍛 submission 📝 on Australia's 📜 draft digital 🖥️ duty 🛡️ of care laws ⚖️ calling the whole thing straight up CENSORSHIP 🚫 of protected 🛡️ speech 🗣️!! Under the proposed rules 📏 tech firms 💻 face massive 💰 fines 💸 if they don't let users 🙋‍♂️ switch 🔄 off algorithms 🤖 in a bid to shield 🛡️ them from harmful ☣️ content 📱 and the US is like nah 🚫 this is government 👮 overreach stretching 🧍‍♂️ its legs 🦵 into viewpoint 🧠 based decisions!! "We ask 🗣️ that Australia 🦘 clarify 🔎 how exactly 'harm' 😣 and 'risks' ⚠️ shall be determined" the embassy wrote ✍️ warning that vague definitions 📖 would let regulators 🧑‍⚖️ impose one-size-fits-all 🧩 platform designs 🏗️ that could globally 🌍 affect what users 👀 see 👁️ say 🗣️ and hear 👂 not just Down Under 🦘 but everywhere 🌐 bro!! "Good to have choice" 🗳️ say regular Aussies 🇦🇺 but Uncle Sam 🦅 is down bad 😩 claiming it risks reducing 📉 the reach 🕸️ of independent 📰 journalists 🗞️ or controversial 🔥 voices 🗣️ if companies pre-emptively demote ⬇️ their stuff!!

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese 🧔‍♂️ clapped back 👏 during his UN 🏛️ visit ✈️ in New York 🗽 telling media 📸 "It's not about giving government 👮 control 🎮 but giving it back 🔄 to individuals 👤" while the US submission 📬 keeps hammering 🛠️ that letting the government enforce 🚨 vague 'harm' definitions 📜 equals viewpoint 🧠 censorship 🚫 of protected 🛡️ speech 🗣️!! They also worried 🤨 the laws 📜 might hurt Australia's rep 🏅 as an innovation 🚀 jurisdiction by scaring off tech bros 💻 with rigid 🪨 platform requirements 📏 that could ripple 🌊 worldwide 🌍 affecting what EVERYONE sees 👀 globally!! The embassy straight up begged 🙏 Australia to address industry fears 😟 that biases 😒 and preferences ❤️ of government officials 👔 could disadvantage 🥉 independent 🆓 or minority-viewpoint 🗣️ speech 🗣️ and the submission even mentioned how this might cook 🍳 the country's innovation street cred 🏙️!!

This spicy 🍵 US criticism 🔥 dropped right as Albanese 🧔‍♂️ was in New York 🗽 speaking at the UN General Assembly 🏛️ about his government's tech policies 📱 and on Tuesday local time ⏰ he responded 📣 by doubling down 🛡️ saying the legislation isn't government overreach 👮 but about handing control 🎛️ back to people over what hits their devices 📲!! Meanwhile President Donald Trump 🧑‍🦰 used his own UN speech 🗣️ to downplay AI 🤖 fears 😱 rejecting guardrails 🛡️ and suggesting we rename it "super intelligence" 🧠 because "artificial" makes it sound fake 🎭!! The US also claimed the opt-out rules 📴 could force tech firms to pre-emptively demote ⬇️ independent journalists 🗞️ whose content touches sensitive topics 🔥 potentially shrinking their global reach 🌍!!

Australia's latest move 🇦🇺 to protect online users 🛡️ from harm ☣️ comes less than a year after they banned social media 📵 for kids under 16 last December ❄️ and now the draft laws 📜 would let everyone opt out 🔄 of algorithms 🤖 so feeds stop force-feeding 🍔 them rage bait 😡 or whatever the platforms push 🚀!! The US embassy submission 📬 warned that mandated platform design features 🛠️ especially around algorithms 🤖 may affect what users see 👁️ say 🗣️ and hear 👂 not just in Australia 🦘 but globally 🌍 which is lowkey a wild 🌪️ reach but they put it in writing ✍️!! They keep stressing that letting the government define 'harm' 😣 and 'risks' ⚠️ risks turning into viewpoint-based 🚫 censorship 🚫 of protected speech 🛡️ and could disadvantage minority voices 🗣️ if officials' biases creep in 😒!!

The submission 📬 also called out that an opt-out option 🔄 would allow regulators 🧑‍⚖️ to impose rigid 🪨 one-size-fits-all 🧩 requirements 📏 on tech firms 💻 potentially hurting innovation 🚀 and Australia's reputation 🏅 as a place that enables wild 🦁 tech growth 🌱!! Albanese 🧔‍♂️ remains firm 💪 insisting it's about giving people control 🎮 over their own devices 📱 rather than governments 👮 pulling strings 🧵 and the US is over here like wait 🛑 this could censor 🛑 protected speech 🗣️ worldwide 🌍 if companies start demoting controversial content 🔥 pre-emptively!! Australians are split 🧩 with some saying "Good to have choice" 🗳️ while the embassy drops these serious concerns 😟 about biases 😒 preferences ❤️ and the global ripple effect 🌊 of one country's algo rules 📜!!
